::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Pythagorean Eqn. with Proportions](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2466360/pythagorean-eqn-with-proportions), asked by [mk mcmahon](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/489917/mk-mcmahon) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-10-10; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> What are the side lengths of a 14" HD screen? This is not trivial to me because the side lengths must remain a 16x9 proportion. 
> Seems like the solution could come from:
>
> ```
> 16a^2+9b^2=196
> ```
>
> I can use this to get the number but I want to see how it's worked out.
> http://screen-size.info/
>
> Like how do the exponents interact with the coefficients? I asked two tutors and they both were stumped....
:::

Let the longer side be $a$.  If the sides have ratio $16:9$, the shorter side has length $\frac{9}{16}a$.  Now
$$a^2 + \left(\frac{9}{16}a\right)^2 = 196$$
and solve for $a$.
